title: What Is Docker & Why Containers?
summary: What a container really is, how it differs from a virtual machine, and how the Docker CLI, the dockerd daemon, containerd, and registries fit together — plus the OCI standard that keeps images portable.

title: Installing Docker & Running Your First Container
summary: Install Docker Engine or Docker Desktop, run hello-world, and read docker ps — then follow a container through its lifecycle from created to running to exited to removed.

title: Images, Tags & Docker Hub
summary: How images are built from layers, what tags and digests mean, and how to pull and push from Docker Hub — including how to tell an official image from the rest.

title: Managing Containers
summary: The everyday container commands: run, stop, start, restart, and rm; running commands inside a container with exec; reading logs; and publishing ports with -p.

title: Your First Dockerfile
summary: Write a Dockerfile with FROM, WORKDIR, COPY, RUN, EXPOSE, and CMD, build it with docker build -t, and understand the build context and .dockerignore.

title: Data Persistence: Volumes & Bind Mounts
summary: Why the container's writable layer is not durable storage, and how named volumes, bind mounts, and tmpfs each keep data — with the commands to create and inspect them.

title: Container Networking Basics
summary: The default bridge versus a user-defined bridge with built-in DNS, the difference between publishing a port and EXPOSE, and how containers reach each other by name.

title: Configuration & the Container Lifecycle
summary: Pass configuration with ENV and --env-file, understand ARG versus ENV, keep containers running with restart policies, and read exit codes and stop signals.

title: Dockerfile Best Practices & Layer Caching
summary: Order instructions so the build cache works for you, use .dockerignore, keep layers lean, pin versions, and choose ENTRYPOINT versus CMD deliberately.

title: Multi-Stage Builds & Small Images
summary: Split a build into stages, copy only the finished artifact with COPY --from, and pick alpine, slim, or distroless base images to shrink size and attack surface.

title: Docker Compose: Multi-Container Apps
summary: Describe a multi-service app in compose.yaml and run it with docker compose up — services, build, image, ports, and volumes, following the current Compose Specification.

title: Compose in Depth
summary: Go beyond the basics: custom networks and volumes, depends_on with healthchecks, profiles, env_file and variable interpolation, and override files.

title: Registries & Tagging Strategies
summary: Push to Docker Hub, GHCR, or a self-hosted registry; log in safely; and adopt a tagging strategy built on immutable digests and meaningful tags rather than latest.

title: Container Security Fundamentals
summary: Run as a non-root USER, apply least privilege, keep secrets out of images and layers, scan images for known vulnerabilities, and start from trusted base images.

title: Logging, Monitoring & Debugging Containers
summary: Use docker logs, stats, inspect, and events to see what a container is doing, add a healthcheck, read exit codes, and debug a container that crashes on start.

title: BuildKit, Buildx & Multi-Platform Images
summary: Understand BuildKit, the default builder, use cache mounts and build secrets, and build images for multiple architectures like amd64 and arm64 with docker buildx.

title: DevOps & the CI/CD Lifecycle
summary: What DevOps means as a culture and a set of practices, the difference between continuous integration, delivery, and deployment, and how containers and the twelve-factor app fit the pipeline.

title: CI/CD with GitHub Actions
summary: Build a workflow that checks out code, runs tests, then builds and pushes a Docker image to GHCR — with build caching, permissions, and secrets handled correctly.

title: Deployment Strategies
summary: Compare recreate, rolling, blue-green, and canary deployments, see why immutable image deploys make rollbacks safe, and use health gates to catch a bad release early.

title: Orchestration Concepts
summary: Why orchestration exists — scheduling, scaling, and self-healing across many hosts — where plain Compose stops being enough, and how Docker Swarm and Kubernetes compare.

title: Introduction to Kubernetes
summary: A conceptual tour of Kubernetes: the control plane and worker nodes, Pods, Deployments, and Services, the kubectl command, and how your Docker image actually runs on a cluster.

title: Infrastructure as Code
summary: Manage infrastructure the way you manage code: declarative versus imperative approaches, why IaC is repeatable and reviewable, config versus secrets, and the GitOps idea.

title: Observability: Logs, Metrics & Health
summary: The three pillars of observability — logs, metrics, and traces — plus structured logging, health and readiness checks, and the Prometheus and Grafana concepts you will meet.

title: Capstone: Containerize, Ship & Operate an App
summary: Tie the whole course together on one app: write its Dockerfile, run it with Compose, ship it through a CI/CD pipeline, deploy it, and watch it in production — with pointers on where to go next.
